claims.text: Equiatomic fcc FeCoNi-based alloys exhibit soft ferromagnetism with high saturation magnetization.
Controlled aging can induce nanoscale chemical and structural heterogeneity in an equiatomic fcc FeCoNi-based alloy.
Nanoscale chemical or structural heterogeneity will increase the coercivity of the alloy.
The coercivity increase will result from domain-wall pinning by fine precipitates or related heterogeneities.
A suitable annealing temperature and duration can form nanoscale precipitates while maintaining the overall fcc structure.
Annealing parameters can be tuned to produce nanoscale heterogeneity without causing a full phase transformation.
The treated material will contain nanoscale precipitates or chemical heterogeneity within an fcc matrix.
The nanoscale precipitates will act as magnetic-anisotropy centers.
The nanoscale precipitates will act as domain-wall pinning sites.
Precipitate-induced anisotropy and domain-wall pinning will increase coercivity relative to untreated FeCoNi-based alloys and FeCoNiPd or FeCoNiPt derivatives.
Controlled aging could increase coercivity by more than 50% relative to the soft-ferromagnetic baseline.
The treated alloy will retain high saturation magnetization.
The treated alloy will retain the fcc structure.
Conventionally processed FeCoNi, FeCoNiPd, and FeCoNiPt are soft ferromagnets with low coercive fields.
Coercivity improvement is expected only when aging creates nanoscale heterogeneity without a detrimental fcc phase change.
Failure to obtain at least a 50% coercivity increase relative to the untreated baseline is defined as a falsifying result.

contradictions.description: The intervention requires annealing at a selected temperature, whereas the conditions state that treatment should occur under ambient conditions. If 'ambient' refers to temperature rather than pressure or atmosphere, these requirements conflict.
